newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds heavy after range break out.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds heavy after range break out.

text.p: *Australian bonds went into the close looking fairly heavy after the market broke down through its recent tight range, sparked off by strong quarterly company profits data.
*Forward bill futures price in policy tightening.
Australian bonds went into the close looking fairly heavy after the market broke down through its recent tight range, leaving the 10-year bond futures contract test key support.
Quarterly company profits for once had an impact on the market, jumping 8.6 percent in December quarter when a flat outcome had been expected, and sparked off the sharp sell-off.

"Yet another sign that the economy has been doing better than earlier thought can only add to the belief that monetary policy is on hold for the indefinite future," said Chris Caton, chief economist at Bankers Trust Australia on the data.

The now more active June bill futures contract is now indicating a cash rate just above current 6.0 percent official interest rates, while the September position is pricing in a 25 basis point policy tightening and December a full half point.

The data reaction gathered momentum once computerised technical accounts, or CTAs, stepped in at just above 92.600 on the March 10-year bond futures contract, which in turn triggered of stop-loss selling.
The contract ended the session testing the 92.550 area a level that has held as support on two occasions earlier this month.

Growing signs of a accelerating economy and concerns over the impact on future inflation ahead of next week's data on enterprise bargaining agreements, and the outcome of the trade union's low paid wage claim next month, also affected sentiment.
Another factor adding to the negative tone was the inability of the U.S. Treasury market to push ahead following a benign CPI reading for Janauary in New York on Wednesday.
The soft tone continued in U.S. debt in Asian trading with Japanese traders reporting investors offloading 10-year notes.
The death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping had no major impact within the dollar bloc debt markets.
The local slide saw the Australian/U.S. 10-year yield spread blow out to over 110 basis points, which some traders see as a buying opportunity. Further resistance seen at 115 basis points.
Margins to Canada reversed an early tightening, while New Zealand debt recaptured some of its recent lost ground.
June bill futures ended the session testing support at 93.93 after breaking through a declining trendline around 94.00, although its relative strength index now close to 25 percent oversold level.
